/**
 * Server-side SFTP proxy for the in-portal file manager.
 *
 * This is a plain (non-"use server") module so it can be imported by both the
 * server actions (lib/actions-files.ts) and the upload/download route handler.
 * It never runs in the browser — the customer's root credentials stay on the
 * server; the browser only ever talks to our own actions/route.
 *
 * Connection target is derived EXACTLY like the server detail page:
 *   - dedicated-IP servers connect to their own IP on port 22
 *   - NAT servers use PUBLIC_IP + the forwarded SSH port
 * Username is always "root"; password is `server.rootPassword`.
 *
 * SANDBOX: on staging (NXEON_SANDBOX=1) no real SSH connection is ever opened —
 * every op is backed by a small in-memory simulated filesystem so the whole
 * file-manager UX works end to end without a live VM.
 */
import SftpClient from "ssh2-sftp-client";
import { SANDBOX } from "./sandbox";
import { decryptSecret } from "./crypto-box";

/**
 * Resolve a server's plaintext root password, preferring the encrypted-at-rest
 * value and falling back to the legacy plaintext column for rows that predate
 * encryption. Every READ of a root password must go through this helper so both
 * shapes keep working transparently.
 */
export function serverRootPassword(
  server: { rootPassword: string | null; rootPasswordEnc?: string | null }
): string | null {
  return decryptSecret(server.rootPasswordEnc) ?? server.rootPassword;
}

/** The minimal shape of a Server we need to open a connection. */
export type SftpServer = {
  id: string;
  rootPassword: string | null;
  rootPasswordEnc?: string | null;
  sshPort: number | null;
  dedicatedIp?: { address: string } | null;
};

export type SftpEntry = {
  name: string;
  /** "d" directory, "-" file, "l" symlink, etc. (ssh2-sftp-client `type`). */
  type: string;
  isDirectory: boolean;
  size: number;
  /** Unix mtime in ms. */
  modifiedMs: number;
  /** Numeric permission bits (e.g. 0o644), or null if unknown. */
  mode: number | null;
};

export type SftpStat = {
  isDirectory: boolean;
  size: number;
  modifiedMs: number;
  mode: number | null;
};

const CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS = 10_000;

/** Max length for any absolute path we accept from the client. */
export const MAX_PATH_LEN = 4096;
/** Max length for a single path segment (file/folder name). */
export const MAX_NAME_LEN = 255;

/**
 * Normalize + validate an absolute POSIX path coming from the browser. Rejects
 * relative paths, `..` traversal, NUL bytes, and over-long paths. Returns a
 * cleaned absolute path (collapsed slashes, resolved `.`), always starting with
 * "/". Throws on anything suspicious — callers surface the message.
 */
export function normalizePath(input: string): string {
  if (typeof input !== "string") throw new Error("Invalid path.");
  if (input.length > MAX_PATH_LEN) throw new Error("Path is too long.");
  if (input.includes("\0")) throw new Error("Invalid path.");
  if (!input.startsWith("/")) throw new Error("Path must be absolute.");

  const out: string[] = [];
  for (const part of input.split("/")) {
    if (part === "" || part === ".") continue;
    if (part === "..") throw new Error("Path traversal is not allowed.");
    if (part.length > MAX_NAME_LEN) throw new Error("A path segment is too long.");
    out.push(part);
  }
  return "/" + out.join("/");
}

/**
 * Validate a single new file/folder name — no slashes, no traversal, no NUL,
 * not "." or "..". Returns the name unchanged if valid.
 */
export function validateName(name: string): string {
  if (typeof name !== "string" || name.length === 0) throw new Error("A name is required.");
  if (name.length > MAX_NAME_LEN) throw new Error("Name is too long.");
  if (name.includes("/") || name.includes("\0")) throw new Error("Name contains invalid characters.");
  if (name === "." || name === "..") throw new Error("That name is not allowed.");
  return name;

# Soul Pilates — PRODUCTION Stack
#
#  Assumes you've copied soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz and
#  soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz onto the host and loaded them with:
#    docker load < soulpilates-backend-latest.tar.gz
#    docker load < soulpilates-frontend-latest.tar.gz
#
#  Then:
#    cp prod.env.sample prod.env  # edit secrets
#    docker compose -f docker-compose.prod.yml up -d
#
#  External access (mongosh / redis-cli from your dev machine):
#    MongoDB → host:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 27117)
#    Redis   → host:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}   (default 6479)
#    Both are auth-protected. Restrict access at the firewall to trusted IPs:
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 27117
#      ufw allow from <your-ip> to any port 6479
# ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

services:

  mongo:
    image: mongo:8
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-mongo
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port so the operator can run mongosh
      # from a dev machine. Auth is mandatory (MONGO_USER / MONGO_PASSWORD).
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${MONGO_PUBLIC_PORT:-27117}:27017"
    environment:
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_USERNAME: ${MONGO_USER}
      MONGO_INITDB_ROOT_PASSWORD: ${MONGO_PASSWORD}
    volumes:
      - ./data/mongo:/data/db
    command: ["mongod", "--bind_ip_all"]
    networks: [internal]

  redis:
    image: redis:7-alpine
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-redis
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      # Exposed on a non-default host port for direct redis-cli access.
      # Protected by REDIS_PASSWORD via --requirepass.
      # Restrict via firewall: ufw allow from <trusted-ip> to any port ${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT}
      - "127.0.0.1:${REDIS_PUBLIC_PORT:-6479}:6379"
    volumes:
      - ./data/redis:/data
    command: ["redis-server", "--appendonly", "yes", "--requirepass", "${REDIS_PASSWORD}"]
    networks: [internal]

  rustfs-volume-init:
    image: alpine:3.20
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs-init
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    command: sh -c "chown -R 10001:10001 /data"
    restart: "no"

  rustfs:
    image: rustfs/rustfs:latest
    container_name: soulpilates-prod-rustfs
    restart: unless-stopped
    ports:
      - "127.0.0.1:6324:9000"      # S3 API — exposed so the public can fetch images
      - "127.0.0.1:6325:9001"
    environment:
      RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY: ${RUSTFS_ACCESS_KEY}
      RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY: ${RUSTFS_SECRET_KEY}
      RUSTFS_CONSOLE_ENABLE: "true"
    volumes:
      - ./data/rustfs:/data
    depends_on:
      rustfs-volume-init:
        condition: service_completed_successfully
    networks: [internal, public]
    healthcheck:
      test: ["CMD", "wget", "--quiet", "--tries=1", "--spider", "http://localhost:9000/health"]
      interval: 5s

## SCENARIO 1 — split the completed/paid class between two instructors

**The single most important finding:** the seat stepper (`− [n] +`) and the "Split into separate people" control **both hard-refuse a cash/card-paid booking** with `BOOKING.ALREADY_PAID` ("Remove and re-add instead") — the guard checks `Attendance.AmountPaid > 0` (SchedulingService `AdjustAttendeeQuantityAsync` / `SplitBookingAsync`). And **Void/Refund never write back to the Attendance** — `AmountPaid` stays 2,000,000 even after you void the invoice. So there is **no admin action that "un-pays" the booking to unlock the stepper.** The supported way to change seats on a paid booking is **Remove + re-Add**, exactly as the error text says. The session being COMPLETED is *not* a blocker and does **not** need un-completing (none of Add-student / Collect / Void check session status).

### Safe click-by-click order

1. **Reverse the payment — use Void, not Refund.** Admin → Invoices → SP-INV-260810-0002 → **🚫 Void** → reason → Confirm. This *deletes* the 2,000,000 CASH payment row, sets invoice VOIDED, and subtracts 2,000,000 from Estela's LifetimeValue (audit log keeps the trail). Void (not Refund) because no cash actually goes back to the customer — it's a re-attribution; Refund would post a phantom −2,000,000 cash-out. Do **not** un-complete the session.

2. **Resize 4→2 on the Nakko class — NOT via the stepper (it will error even after voiding).** On the class-detail panel: **🗑 Remove** Estela's booking (frees all 4 seats, deletes the attendance; no credits involved — it was cash), then use the **Add-student bar with the seat-qty input = 2** to re-add Estela. This creates a fresh **unpaid** PAY_AT_STUDIO booking, Qty 2, due 500,000×2 = 1,000,000, Status BOOKED. Set status back to **Arrived**. (Side effect: re-adding fires a booking-confirmation email to Estela.)

3. **Create Session B (Linna), same date/time.** Calendar → click the 11:00 slot / **Add Class** → New Session modal → Date&Start `2026-08-10 11:00`, Duration 55, Capacity 2, Blueprint = the "Sculpt Waist" blueprint (`6a476294088d62bf2e9df8a8`), **Instructor = Linna** → Create. (Posts to `session/manual`; blueprint copies GROUP + 500,000 price; instructor overridden to Linna.)

4. **Add Estela ×2 to Session B** via its Add-student bar (qty 2). Unpaid, due 1,000,000. Mark Arrived.

5. **Collect cash on each.** Each unpaid booking now shows a **🛒 Checkout / 💰 Collect** button → Collect modal → amount **1,000,000**, method **Cash** → confirm. Creates a PAID invoice + CASH payment per session and stamps AmountPaid. Do it on both the Nakko booking and the Linna booking.

**End state:** two sessions, Estela ×2 each, each with its own PAID cash invoice of 1,000,000 (total 2,000,000, unchanged); original invoice VOIDED. LifetimeValue nets back to original (−2M then +1M +1M).

### Commission / risk callouts
- Commission is computed at **payroll-run time**, per session, keyed to the session's InstructorId, from attendees who **ARRIVED *and* PAID** (PayrollService `IsAttendancePaidAsync`, SPM-113). So the split works — Nakko's session bills 2 paid seats at Nakko's rate, Linna's new session bills 2 paid seats at Linna's rate — **only if each seat ends up both Arrived and cash-collected.** Any seat left unpaid counts toward *neither* instructor.
- Voiding the original invoice does not corrupt commission (it isn't read off the old invoice). Between void and re-collect the booking is momentarily unpaid; only the final paid state matters at the run.
- Minor: BookingReference SP-260808-9901 disappears with the removed attendance; re-adds mint new refs and send confirmation emails.

## SCENARIO 2 — backdated private class + the 250,000 commission question

### (a) Safe UI steps
- **Create client Hannah:** Admin → Clients → New (ClientController `POST /api/client`). Supported.
- **Backdated PRIVATE session Aug 9 2026 16:00, Nakko:** Calendar → Add Class → datetime-local = `2026-08-09 16:00` → Blueprint = a PRIVATE one (below) → Instructor Nakko → Capacity 1 → Create. **Past dates ARE allowed** — the `datetime-local` field has no `min`, and `CreateManualSessionAsync` performs **no future-date validation**.
- **Book Hannah + cash 850,000:** open the session → Add-student → Hannah (qty 1; private duo cap is 2) → **🛒 Checkout** → 850,000, method **Cash** → confirm (PAID invoice + CASH payment). Mark Arrived (required for commission).

### (b) Available PRIVATE class types
Two blueprints, both **PRIVATE / ALL_LEVELS / 850,000 VND / default instructor Nakko**: **"Private Class"** (`6a476a8e…`) and **"Private Session"** (`6a476ccb…`). The 850,000 matches the scenario's cash amount.

### (c) The 250,000 per-class commission override — the precise answer
**There is NO per-class commission override in the admin UI.**
- `Attendance.ImportedCommissionAmount` is a genuine per-class verbatim-override field (payroll short-circuits to it when set), **but it is written ONLY by the historical spreadsheet importer** (SoulPilates.Migration). No controller, service, or Astro page ever sets it — it is read-only in the running app. Setting it for this one class would require a direct Mongo write to that attendance (out-of-UI) or a code change to expose it.
- The only rate override the UI offers is **`MonthlyCommissionOverride`** (Staff → commission-overrides; StaffController CRUD) — **per-staff, per-MONTH**. It would rewrite the rate for *every* class Nakko taught that month, so it cannot isolate one class. Wrong granularity.
- The ClassDetailPanel shows commission **read-only** ("Class completed — commission finalised", model/rate/tier) — no editable field.

**The supported mechanism for a one-off "Sunday bonus" is the ad-hoc Bonus feature** (Admin → Expenses → "Bonuses & Reimb." tab → **Record bonus**; AccountingController `POST /api/accounting/bonuses`): recipient Nakko, Year 2026 / Month 8, amount **250,000**, reason "Sunday bonus". The `Bonus` entity's own doc literally uses the "250K" example. It adds 250,000 to Nakko's monthly payable via the washout. **Caveat:** this is *additive* — it sits on top of whatever the class's normal computed commission is; it does not *replace* the class's commission. If the operator specifically wants this class's computed commission to *read* exactly 250,000 (replacing the rate), that is the unsupported case above and needs a backend write or code change.
